properties.name: FIXED — the stale-lock reclaim admitted two winners because its check and its unlink were two steps; it is now serialized by a guard, 10/60 trials became 0/60
properties.statement:
FIXED 2026-09-13. Supersedes this record's original reading, which named the mechanism correctly and had not measured it.

① SYMPTOM. tools/test_loop_nudge.py::test_a_stale_lock_is_reclaimed_exactly_once, "AssertionError: 2 != 1". Intermittent: roughly 2 in 9 full-suite runs, and 0 in 20 when that test ran ALONE. Surfaced in CI on a commit that touched only AGENTS.md, which is what made it worth diagnosing rather than re-running.

② PRECEDENT. Searched; nothing in the design but this record. New.

③ CANDIDATES, generated rather than assumed:
   (a) the loser's unlink deletes the winner's fresh lock — needs a genuinely stale pre-existing lock
   (b) ANY brand-new lock is briefly readable as stale: O_CREAT|O_EXCL makes an EMPTY file and the payload is a separate os.write, and _probe_lock_is_stale returns True for an unreadable file
   (c) the observation is wrong and the harness double-counts

④⑤ THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, and it is the reason this is settled rather than argued. (b) predicts failure with NO pre-existing lock; (a) predicts failure only with one. 8 processes released on a barrier under CPU load, 60 trials per arm:

        pre-seeded STALE lock    10/60 trials had != 1 winner   (2 and 3)
        NO lock at all            0/60

   (b) REFUTED. (a) CONFIRMED. (c) refuted by the same arms — the harness counts 1 correctly 60 times running.

⑥ THE CLASS. Check-then-act, and the instance-not-class pattern in its purest form: claim_probe_slot's OWN docstring records that it replaced "a check-then-write pair that read as a guard and was not one", measured at four probes from twelve invocations. That fix corrected the common path and left a SECOND check-then-act inside its own error branch.

⑦ PINNED BY TESTS THAT FAIL TODAY, verified by reverting the fix and watching them go red — and the first attempt at one of them WAS A TEST THAT COULD NOT FAIL. It put a FRESH lock in place and asserted the reclaim declines; both the old and new shapes decline, because a fresh lock is not stale. It passed against the unfixed code. What the fix actually guarantees is MUTUAL EXCLUSION, so the test now asserts that: a reclaim attempted while another is in progress must decline and leave the stale lock untouched. Both new tests fail against the reverted code and pass against the fix.

⑧ THE FIX, at the cause. _reclaim_stale_probe_lock serializes reclaimers behind an O_EXCL guard and re-checks staleness INSIDE that section, so a straggler finds a fresh lock and declines instead of deleting it. An orphaned guard (a process killed mid-reclaim) is cleared once and the attempt declines anyway, so the next invocation reclaims — one-shot, never a retry loop, because a wedged guard must cost one skipped probe rather than a spin.

RESULT: stress harness 10/60 -> 0/60. Full suite 0 failures in 12 consecutive runs, against roughly 2 in 9 before.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how often this fired in real use rather than under a barrier — real hook invocations are near-simultaneous but not synchronised, so the true rate is unknown and probably far below 1 in 6. The cost when it did fire is known and is not trivial: a duplicate loop_status probe, which the first usage ledger priced at 71.4% of all time this project spent inside reflow2.
